correctness.rationale: For m>4 every abstract isomorphism preserves the four-vertex shore. Deleting just the larger-shore leaves preserves connectivity and retains every hub. The larger-shore excess degree is three, whose partitions give one degree-four center, a degree-three and degree-two pair sharing exactly one hub, or three degree-two vertices whose suppression gives the star or path on four hubs. The corresponding full hub actions are S4, a single swap, S3 and a double swap. Two leaf attachments yield isomorphic trees precisely when their multiplicity vectors lie in the same orbit. The four cycle-index contributions give the stated rational series; their fourth-order pole factor at 1 is 29/24 and the poles elsewhere have smaller order and orders dividing 12 as roots of unity. The independent replay generates all unlabelled trees up to order 14 by adjoining a leaf and canonicalizing by the minimal rooted encoding over all roots. Every tree is produced because deleting any leaf yields a smaller tree; equal minimal rooted codes characterize isomorphism. Filtering by shore size gives 28,45,73,105,152,204 with the predicted four core counts separately, and exact algebra confirms the rational form and leading coefficient 29/144. The independent finite replay is a cross-check, not the all-order proof.
residual_risks: No inference is made about balanced shores, in which an uncoloured isomorphism can interchange them.

originality.rationale: A distinct earlier Resultary finding proves the exact finite-core Burnside coefficient formula on the identical abstract tree invariant for all fixed d≥2 and m>d. Substitution d=4 specializes its very same core and orbit classification, giving the four contributions by the elementary partitions of three, hence the exact rational series and period bound even though the earlier source did not print the reduced fraction. This is verified general-theorem coverage, not an inference from an inaccessible thesis or from a title match.
residual_risks: The thesis may settle the earlier history of the explicit four-shore expression, but is not needed to demonstrate existing exact theorem coverage. No claim that the printed reduced fraction was located in an earlier text.
